html:
The Pipil are the Nahua people of western and central El Salvador. They speak Nawat, a language close to the Nahuatl of central Mexico, and descend from Nahua groups who moved south into Central America several centuries before the Spanish came.

Their main state, Cuzcatlán, had its capital near today's San Salvador. They grew maize and large crops of cacao, which was traded across Mesoamerica. Their neighbours were the Lenca to the east and the Xinca to the west.

In 1524 Pedro de Alvarado invaded from Guatemala and, after hard fighting, the Spanish took the country. In 1932 an uprising in the west of El Salvador was crushed in the massacre known as La Matanza, in which thousands of Indigenous people were killed. Fear afterwards led many to stop speaking Nawat in public, and only a few speakers remain. See also Nicarao.
